newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar up on short-covering, top at 111.30-40 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar up on short-covering, top at 111.30-40 yen.

text.p: *Dollar was firmer against yen in Tokyo morning on surge of short-covering from operators who had sold earlier, including interbank and overseas operators as well as Japanese life insurers.
*Impetus for short-covering provided by October trade figures, with overall surplus failing to show increase. But surplus with U.S. rose, helping to keep topside intact.
*Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus fell 12.9 percent in October from year ago to 470.86 billion yen, 23rd consecutive month it has declined on year-on-year basis.
*Reuters poll of economists had produced an average forecast of surplus of 570 billion yen for October.
*Surplus with United States rose 31.3 percent to 354.79 billion yen in October from a year earlier.
*Topside expected to be limited to around 111.30-40 yen, where profit-taking likely to emerge.
*Market waiting for comments from visiting U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, who is due to meet Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka at 0110 GMT.
*He is also due to meet Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita and to make speech later in day.
